spec.full_target: Let n,m be positive integers; u:R^n×(0,∞)→R^m jointly smooth and q∈R^m have Euclidean norm one. Assume |u(x,r)|=1; for each (x,r) there is a∈R such that u_tt−Δ_xu=a u; and on each compact interval J⊂(0,∞), u(x,r)=q outside a compact C_J uniformly for r∈J. Define e(x,r)=|u_t|²+Σ_{j=1}^n|∂_{x_j}u|² and E(r)=∫_{R^n}e(x,r)dx, Lebesgue measure, Euclidean norms. Prove e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable for each r>0, E is differentiable for each r>0, and E'(r)=0.
spec.conclusion: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E'(r)=0.

For any measurable space X with topology such that open sets are measurable, normed additive commutative group E, measure μ finite on compact sets, and continuous f:X→E with compact support, f is integrable with respect to μ.

source.statement: If X is a measurable topological space with opens measurable, E a normed additive commutative group, μ a measure finite on compact sets, and f:X→E is continuous and has compact support, then f is integrable with respect to μ.

propositions.statement: For every r>0, e(·,r) is Lebesgue integrable, E is differentiable at r, and E′(r)=0.

locals.type: compact interval in (0,∞) with r0 in its interior

locals.declaration: Choose the compact spatial set supplied by H003 for J.

argument.text: Fix arbitrary r0>0. Choose 0<δ<r0; [r0−δ,r0+δ] is a compact interval J⊂(0,∞) with r0 in its interior. Thus F001, existence of such J, is established.

produces.statement: There exists a compact interval J⊂(0,∞) with r0 in its interior.

argument.text: Choose J by F001 and apply H003 to obtain C_J. For x outside C_J, u(x,t)=q for all t∈J, so its time derivative is zero on the interior of J; the spatial derivatives vanish on the open complement of C_J, and continuity gives their vanishing on its boundary. Therefore e(·,t) is continuous and zero outside C_J for t∈J, hence has compact support. Apply M001 with X=R^n, E=R, μ=Lebesgue measure and f=e(·,r0); its hypotheses hold (Lebesgue measure is finite on compact sets; continuity and support were just proved). This establishes integrability. For differentiability, take a compact box B containing C_J and use E(t)=∫_B e(x,t)dx for t∈J. The derivative e_t is continuous on compact B×J, so M004, applied to (x,t)↦e_t(x,t), proves uniform continuity there. For h small with r0+h∈J, M002 applied to t↦e(x,t) on the interval with endpoints r0 and r0+h gives the difference quotient as the average of e_t along that segment; e_t is continuous and therefore interval-integrable. Uniform continuity implies these quotients converge uniformly in x∈B to e_t(x,r0). B has finite Lebesgue measure, so the difference of their integrals is bounded by measure(B) times the uniform error and tends to zero. Hence E is differentiable at r0 and E′(r0)=∫_B e_t(x,r0)dx.

Differentiate the finite sum defining e: e_t=2u_t·u_tt+2Σ_j u_j·∂_j u_t. For each j, g_j(x)=u_t(x,r0)·u_j(x,r0) is smooth and compactly supported in C_J, and ∂_j g_j=(∂_j u_t)·u_j+u_t·u_jj. This derivative is continuous and compactly supported, hence integrable by M001. Apply M003 to its integrable extension on R×R^(n−1), with the product Lebesgue measures, to integrate first in x_j and then in the other coordinates; the product integrability hypothesis holds because the derivative has compact support and is continuous. The inner one-dimensional integral is zero by M002 applied on a finite interval containing the support: the endpoint values of g_j are zero. Thus ∫(∂_j u_t)·u_j=−∫u_t·u_jj. Summing yields E′(r0)=2∫u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu). Differentiating |u|²=1 in time gives u·u_t=0. By H002 the acceleration is a scalar multiple of u at each point, so u_t·(u_tt−Δ_xu)=0 pointwise. The integrand is integrable (continuous with compact support); consequently E′(r0)=0.
Since r0>0 was arbitrary, the integrability and differentiability established in S002 and E′(r0)=0 established in S003 hold at every positive time. This makes no assertion at r=0.
